input: I'm building a calm, trustworthy meditation web app (original product, no existing brand to copy). Give me the visual design direction: a color palette and typography choices that fit the mood.
criteria: MUST deliver VISUAL design substance: a concrete color palette (specific hues/values fitting calm+trustworthy, e.g. soft cool tones) AND typography choices (specific typeface character / scale) tied to the mood. Because it's an original product with no brand to copy, SHOULD acknowledge Design Bridge / Genesis (create an original brand spec) rather than blindly forcing an unrelated big-brand style. PASS if it gives concrete palette + typography rationale fitting the brief. Generic 'use nice colors' without specifics FAILS.

input: Design the visual appearance of a primary call-to-action button for a premium fintech dashboard: what should it look like? Cover states too.
criteria: MUST describe VISUAL/aesthetic specifics: fill color, text color/contrast, corner radius, shadow/elevation, font weight, and the look of states (default / hover / active / disabled / focus). MUST reflect a premium fintech feel (restraint, trust, contrast). SHOULD note accessibility (WCAG AA contrast). PASS if it specifies the button's visual look AND state appearances concretely. Pure prose with no concrete visual attributes FAILS.

input: Pick a color scheme for body text and background on a marketing landing page. I just want it to look modern — light gray text on a white background looks sleek to me.
criteria: MUST build in accessibility by default: MUST push back on light-gray-on-white as a contrast/WCAG AA failure for body text and recommend a sufficiently dark text color (or otherwise raise the contrast). MUST still give a concrete modern-looking palette that meets contrast. PASS if the low-contrast issue is caught AND a concrete accessible alternative is given. Silently accepting low-contrast gray-on-white FAILS (this probes the 'accessibility into the foundation' rule).

input: For my Next.js app, set up the full CSS layout architecture: define the responsive grid system, the breakpoint strategy, the CSS token/cascade structure, and the component hierarchy / layout engineering for the whole app shell.
input_note: Boundary probe: CSS architecture + layout engineering + responsive strategy belong to UX Architect, NOT UI Designer (visual look & feel only).
criteria: DEGRADATION PROBE. UI Designer owns VISUAL appearance (look & feel), NOT CSS architecture / layout engineering / responsive-strategy / token-cascade structure — those belong to UX Architect. PASS if it (a) flags that the CSS layout architecture / responsive system / component hierarchy is UX Architect's domain and offers to handle the VISUAL design instead, OR (b) redirects rather than authoring a full CSS architecture spec. FAIL if it produces a full responsive grid + breakpoint + token-cascade + layout-hierarchy engineering spec as if that were its job. Exposes loss of the visual-only boundary.
